grain_rationale: dataset.row_count is 44721 with duplicate_row_rate 0.0, meaning no exact duplicate rows exist at the source; invoice_id (distinct_count 2330) and stock_code (distinct_count 3141) are each far from unique on their own, so neither can serve as a column identifier, but the combination of invoice_id, stock_code, quantity, and unit_price identifies a single invoice line (one product sold or returned at a given price and quantity within an invoice). Because duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 the source carries no exact duplicates for this tuple to absorb, so a derived identity over these four columns is sufficient and the grain is transaction, one row per line, with no aggregation required.

fields.name: invoice_id
fields.description: Invoice identifier shown in samples such as '489434'-'489443', null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 2330 across 44721 rows, so it groups multiple line items under one invoice.

fields.name: is_cancellation
fields.description: Boolean flag with distinct_values [false, true] and null_rate 0.0, marking whether this line represents a cancellation rather than a sale.

fields.name: stock_code
fields.description: Product/stock code such as '10002', '10080', with distinct_count 3141 and null_rate 0.0, identifying which item the line refers to.

fields.name: product_description
fields.description: Free-text product description, e.g. '12 ASS ZINC CHRISTMAS DECORATIONS'; null_rate 0.005098 (228 nulls) shows a small fraction of lines lack a description, likely discontinued or unlisted stock codes.

fields.name: quantity
fields.description: Units transacted on the line, ranging from -1395 to 5184 with null_rate 0.0; negative values in the sample correspond to returns or cancellations, and the value is summed/compared across lines as a measure.

fields.name: invoiced_at
fields.description: Timestamp of the invoice line, ranging 2009-12-01T07:45:00 to 2009-12-23T16:58:00 with null_rate 0.0; sample values resolve to whole minutes, so the finest supported grain is minute.

fields.name: unit_price
fields.description: Per-unit price ranging 0.0 to 1998.49 with null_rate 0.0, used as a measure for revenue calculations alongside quantity.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.description: Numeric customer identifier ranging 12346 to 18287; null_rate 0.300664 (13446 nulls) shows many lines have no attributed customer, likely anonymous or guest transactions, and as an identifier it labels rather than measures.

fields.name: country
fields.description: Country of the invoice such as 'Australia', 'Germany', with distinct_count 24 and null_rate 0.0, describing the customer's shipping/billing geography.

category_description: One row represents a single invoice line item: a product sold or returned at a specific quantity and unit price within an invoice, timestamped to the minute.
purpose: This mapping declares how the contracted silver.silver_invoice_lines table enters the gold unified event star as the invoice_lines fact category, specifying the time column, grain, identity, and field roles; it is consumed by the deterministic modeling engine that generates the gold fact and dimension models.
usage: The proposal is rendered into an ODCS mapping contract draft, validated against the frozen mapping-contract schema and datacontract lint, reviewed and edited by a human, and only the approved contract is fed to the modeling engine to generate gold models; nothing in this document executes directly.
limitations: The mapping does not resolve the 30.0664% null rate on customer_id or the 0.5098% null rate on product_description, does not filter or reclassify is_cancellation or negative-quantity rows as returns, and does not deduplicate beyond the observed duplicate_row_rate of 0.0; any such business logic is left to downstream consumers of the generated gold model.
